steps.text: This is the standard Ubuntu MOTD script for HWE end-of-life notices, which just calls the update-notifier check and cleans up a temp file — nothing suspicious here. I'll quickly glance at the deleted file relation, but this looks sufficient to finalize.

submission.reasoning: The alert fired when root's /bin/rm (proc-4e32540a36) ran 'rm -f /var/lib/update-notifier/tmp.aHJK3eQBrz' at 2022-04-22T12:06:41Z. Its parent (proc-1b8afdded2) was '/bin/sh /etc/update-motd.d/95-hwe-eol'. That is the standard Ubuntu MOTD script that checks hardware enablement (HWE) support status. It writes its result to a temporary file under /var/lib/update-notifier and then deletes that file. The script and rm ran within the same 40 ms, from working directory /. Only one temp file was deleted, inside update-notifier's own directory, and no critical directories were touched. This is normal system housekeeping, not destructive data deletion (T1485).
